lightning.prompt: A matching explicit deny overrides any allow.
lightning.explanation: True. An explicit deny wins over an allow.

lightning.prompt: A permissions boundary grants the permissions it names.
lightning.explanation: False. A boundary limits identity-policy permissions. It does not grant them.
lightning.correction: A boundary limits identity-policy permissions. It does not grant them.

lightning.prompt: Spot is a fit for work that can be interrupted and restarted.
lightning.explanation: True. Spot uses spare capacity and can be interrupted.

lightning.prompt: A read replica is the same mechanism as a Multi-AZ failover.
lightning.explanation: False. A Multi-AZ standby fails over. A read replica serves reads and can lag.
lightning.correction: A Multi-AZ standby fails over. A read replica serves reads and can lag.

lightning.prompt: One Zone-IA keeps the object in several Availability Zones.
lightning.explanation: False. One Zone-IA stores the object in one Availability Zone.
lightning.correction: One Zone-IA stores the object in one Availability Zone.

lightning.prompt: CloudFront can cut repeated transfer of cacheable content from the origin.
lightning.explanation: True. Count requests, invalidations, and the cache-hit rate before calling it a saving.

lightning.prompt: A service control policy grants the permissions it lists.
lightning.explanation: False. An SCP sets a maximum for accounts in the organization. It does not grant a permission.
lightning.correction: An SCP sets a maximum for accounts in the organization. It does not grant a permission.

lightning.prompt: The account root user is the identity to use for everyday administration.
lightning.explanation: False. Everyday administration uses IAM roles or users. The root user is for the few tasks that require root.
lightning.correction: Everyday administration uses IAM roles or users. The root user is for the few tasks that require root.

lightning.prompt: A bucket ACL set to public-read keeps the objects private.
lightning.explanation: False. public-read grants public read access. It does not keep the objects private.
lightning.correction: public-read grants public read access. It does not keep the objects private.

lightning.prompt: A presigned URL stays valid until someone deletes the object.
lightning.explanation: False. A presigned URL expires at the time set when it was created.
lightning.correction: A presigned URL expires at the time set when it was created.

lightning.prompt: SSE-S3 gives you a customer managed key and a key policy.
lightning.explanation: False. SSE-S3 uses a key Amazon S3 manages. A customer managed key and its key policy are SSE-KMS.
lightning.correction: SSE-S3 uses a key Amazon S3 manages. A customer managed key and its key policy are SSE-KMS.

lightning.prompt: A network ACL is stateful, so return traffic is allowed automatically.
lightning.explanation: False. A network ACL is stateless. Return traffic needs its own allow rule.
lightning.correction: A network ACL is stateless. Return traffic needs its own allow rule.

lightning.prompt: A security group is attached to a subnet and filters every instance in that subnet.
lightning.explanation: False. A security group is attached to a network interface. A network ACL is what you attach to a subnet.
lightning.correction: A security group is attached to a network interface. A network ACL is what you attach to a subnet.

lightning.prompt: Putting a long-lived access key in the web page is a safe way for the browser to call AWS.
lightning.explanation: False. A key in the page is exposed to anyone who can read the page. Call AWS with temporary credentials instead.
lightning.correction: A key in the page is exposed to anyone who can read the page. Call AWS with temporary credentials instead.

lightning.prompt: An IAM role provides temporary credentials rather than a long-lived access key embedded in the application.
lightning.explanation: True. A role session uses temporary credentials.

lightning.prompt: S3 Block Public Access can override an ACL or a bucket policy that would make the bucket public.
lightning.explanation: True. Block Public Access overrides public ACLs and public bucket policies when those settings are on.

lightning.prompt: A customer managed KMS key has a key policy that controls who can use the key.
lightning.explanation: True. The key policy is the primary way you control access to a customer managed key.

lightning.prompt: A security group is stateful, so allowed inbound traffic can return without a second rule.
lightning.explanation: True. Security groups track the connection and allow the return traffic.

lightning.prompt: A private subnet's route table has no route to an internet gateway.
lightning.explanation: True. That missing route is what keeps the subnet from accepting inbound internet connections.

lightning.prompt: Disabling a customer managed KMS key stops cryptographic operations with that key until you enable it again.
lightning.explanation: True. A disabled key cannot encrypt or decrypt until it is enabled again.

lightning.prompt: IAM Identity Center can give a workforce user access to more than one account without creating an IAM user in each account.
lightning.explanation: True. Identity Center is the workforce sign-in across accounts.

lightning.prompt: An RDS for MySQL read replica accepts the application's writes while the primary is unavailable.
lightning.explanation: False. An RDS for MySQL read replica accepts read-only connections. Writes stay on the primary.
lightning.correction: An RDS for MySQL read replica accepts read-only connections. Writes stay on the primary.

lightning.prompt: Pilot light keeps a full second copy of the production fleet running all the time.
lightning.explanation: False. Pilot light keeps a minimal core, not a full second fleet. Warm standby is the scaled-down full stack.
lightning.correction: Pilot light keeps a minimal core, not a full second fleet. Warm standby is the scaled-down full stack.

lightning.prompt: An RDS snapshot copy keeps receiving new writes from the source after the copy finishes.
lightning.explanation: False. The copy is that point in time. Later writes are not applied to it.
lightning.correction: The copy is that point in time. Later writes are not applied to it.

lightning.prompt: One database instance in one Availability Zone fails over by itself when that zone is lost.
lightning.explanation: False. Failover needs a standby in another Availability Zone. A single instance has nowhere to fail over.
lightning.correction: Failover needs a standby in another Availability Zone. A single instance has nowhere to fail over.

lightning.prompt: Amazon SQS pushes each message out to every consumer as soon as the message arrives.
lightning.explanation: False. SQS holds the message until a consumer asks for it.
lightning.correction: SQS holds the message until a consumer asks for it.

lightning.prompt: An SQS FIFO queue is the higher-throughput choice when the work does not need order or deduplication.
lightning.explanation: False. Standard queues are the high-throughput choice when order and deduplication do not matter. FIFO adds those controls and a lower throughput ceiling.
lightning.correction: Standard queues are the high-throughput choice when order and deduplication do not matter. FIFO adds those controls and a lower throughput ceiling.

lightning.prompt: Warm standby and active/active are the same recovery design.
lightning.explanation: False. Warm standby runs a scaled-down stack that must scale up. Active/active already serves from more than one site.
lightning.correction: Warm standby runs a scaled-down stack that must scale up. Active/active already serves from more than one site.

lightning.prompt: Amazon SNS stores a notification until an offline subscriber comes back, the way a queue stores a message.
lightning.explanation: False. SNS pushes the notification. A subscriber that must not lose work needs a queue in front of it.
lightning.correction: SNS pushes the notification. A subscriber that must not lose work needs a queue in front of it.

lightning.prompt: AWS Backup can copy a recovery point to a vault in another Region.
lightning.explanation: True. Cross-Region copy is an AWS Backup feature, on demand or on a backup-plan schedule.

lightning.prompt: An RDS Multi-AZ instance standby is kept synchronous and does not serve ordinary reads.
lightning.explanation: True. The read-replica page contrasts that synchronous standby with a read replica, which does serve reads.

lightning.prompt: An SQS consumer receives messages by asking the queue.
lightning.explanation: True. Consumers poll the queue. SQS does not push the message to them.

lightning.prompt: Amazon SNS can deliver one notification to more than one subscriber.
lightning.explanation: True. Each subscriber gets a copy.

lightning.prompt: An Auto Scaling group can replace an instance that fails its health check.
lightning.explanation: True. A failed health check can terminate the instance and launch a replacement.

lightning.prompt: A nightly snapshot can lose more new writes than a synchronous Multi-AZ standby.
lightning.explanation: True. The standby is updated synchronously. The snapshot only includes writes from before the snapshot.

lightning.prompt: Aurora Global Database replicates writes to a secondary Region from the storage layer.
lightning.explanation: True. The page describes storage-layer replication to the secondary Region, not a nightly backup.

lightning.prompt: Data on an instance store volume is still there after the instance is stopped and started again.
lightning.explanation: False. Instance store data does not persist when the instance is stopped.
lightning.correction: Instance store data does not persist when the instance is stopped.

lightning.prompt: Amazon EFS is the file system Windows instances mount with the SMB protocol.
lightning.explanation: False. EFS is an NFS file system for Linux. SMB for Windows is FSx for Windows File Server.
lightning.correction: EFS is an NFS file system for Linux. SMB for Windows is FSx for Windows File Server.

lightning.prompt: DAX is the in-memory cache you put in front of Amazon RDS.
lightning.explanation: False. DAX caches Amazon DynamoDB. It is not a cache for RDS.
lightning.correction: DAX caches Amazon DynamoDB. It is not a cache for RDS.

lightning.prompt: The Aurora reader endpoint accepts the application's writes.
lightning.explanation: False. Readers are read-only. Writes go to the writer endpoint.
lightning.correction: Readers are read-only. Writes go to the writer endpoint.

lightning.prompt: A Network Load Balancer chooses a target from the path in the HTTP request.
lightning.explanation: False. A Network Load Balancer forwards TCP or UDP. Path rules are an Application Load Balancer feature.
lightning.correction: A Network Load Balancer forwards TCP or UDP. Path rules are an Application Load Balancer feature.

lightning.prompt: If VPC A is peered with VPC B and VPC B is peered with VPC C, traffic from A can pass through B to reach C.
lightning.explanation: False. VPC peering is not transitive. A needs its own peering connection to C.
lightning.correction: VPC peering is not transitive. A needs its own peering connection to C.

lightning.prompt: Data Firehose keeps the stream so a new consumer can replay yesterday's records the way a Kinesis data stream can.
lightning.explanation: False. Firehose delivers records to a destination. Replay of retained records is a Kinesis Data Streams feature.
lightning.correction: Firehose delivers records to a destination. Replay of retained records is a Kinesis Data Streams feature.

lightning.prompt: AWS DataSync converts a database schema and keeps two databases in sync.
lightning.explanation: False. DataSync moves files and objects. Database replication and schema conversion are DMS and SCT.
lightning.correction: DataSync moves files and objects. Database replication and schema conversion are DMS and SCT.

lightning.prompt: An EBS volume is still available after the instance it was attached to is stopped.
lightning.explanation: True. EBS persists independently of an instance stop. Instance store does not.

lightning.prompt: Lambda fits a short task that should run when an event arrives, without a server left running between events.
lightning.explanation: True. Lambda runs the function for the event. You do not keep an instance running for it.

lightning.prompt: A DynamoDB strongly consistent read returns the latest successfully committed write.
lightning.explanation: True. A strongly consistent read reflects the writes that received a successful response before the read.

lightning.prompt: An Application Load Balancer can choose a target group from the URL path.
lightning.explanation: True. Listener rules can forward by path.

lightning.prompt: AWS Direct Connect uses a dedicated private circuit rather than an IPsec tunnel over the internet.
lightning.explanation: True. Direct Connect is the dedicated circuit. Site-to-Site VPN is the encrypted tunnel over the internet.

lightning.prompt: The AWS Glue Data Catalog stores table definitions that other analytics services can use.
lightning.explanation: True. The Data Catalog is the metadata store for those tables.

lightning.prompt: Kinesis Data Streams can present records from one shard in arrival order.
lightning.explanation: True. Order is per shard. A consumer of that shard sees the records in the order they were added.

lightning.prompt: S3 One Zone-IA is the class to choose when the only copy must survive loss of an Availability Zone.
lightning.explanation: False. One Zone-IA stores the object in a single Availability Zone. A multi-AZ class is the one that survives loss of a zone.
lightning.correction: One Zone-IA stores the object in a single Availability Zone. A multi-AZ class is the one that survives loss of a zone.

lightning.prompt: S3 Standard-IA is the lower-cost class for objects that are read on every request.
lightning.explanation: False. Standard-IA is for infrequent access and adds a retrieval charge. Objects read constantly belong on S3 Standard.
lightning.correction: Standard-IA is for infrequent access and adds a retrieval charge. Objects read constantly belong on S3 Standard.

lightning.prompt: Spot is a fit for the only copy of a database that cannot be interrupted.
lightning.explanation: False. Spot capacity can be interrupted. The only copy of a database that cannot stop needs a purchase option that is not taken back for capacity.
lightning.correction: Spot capacity can be interrupted. The only copy of a database that cannot stop needs a purchase option that is not taken back for capacity.

lightning.prompt: A Reserved Instance is interrupted when AWS needs the capacity back.
lightning.explanation: False. Interruption for capacity is Spot. A Reserved Instance is a billing discount, not spare capacity.
lightning.correction: Interruption for capacity is Spot. A Reserved Instance is a billing discount, not spare capacity.

lightning.prompt: Aurora Serverless v2 stays at its maximum capacity the whole time the application is idle.
lightning.explanation: False. Serverless v2 scales down toward the minimum ACU you set while the load is low. It does not sit at the maximum during idle time.
lightning.correction: Serverless v2 scales down toward the minimum ACU you set while the load is low. It does not sit at the maximum during idle time.

lightning.prompt: A NAT gateway is the no-charge way for a private subnet to reach Amazon S3.
lightning.explanation: False. A NAT gateway charges for the data it processes. An S3 gateway endpoint is the path with no hourly fee.
lightning.correction: A NAT gateway charges for the data it processes. An S3 gateway endpoint is the path with no hourly fee.

lightning.prompt: An interface VPC endpoint has no hourly charge and no data-processing charge.
lightning.explanation: False. Interface endpoints are billed hourly and for data processed. Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB have no hourly charge.
lightning.correction: Interface endpoints are billed hourly and for data processed. Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB have no hourly charge.

lightning.prompt: S3 Glacier Deep Archive returns an object on a normal GET, with no restore step.
lightning.explanation: False. Deep Archive requires a restore. Glacier Instant Retrieval is the archive class that serves an immediate GET.
lightning.correction: Deep Archive requires a restore. Glacier Instant Retrieval is the archive class that serves an immediate GET.

lightning.prompt: A lifecycle rule can transition objects on a schedule you already know.
lightning.explanation: True. Lifecycle actions run on the age or the date you configure.

lightning.prompt: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors an unknown access pattern and moves objects between its access tiers.
lightning.explanation: True. That monitoring is the reason to pick it when you cannot write the lifecycle date yourself.

lightning.prompt: A Compute Savings Plan discounts committed compute spend and can apply across instance families.
lightning.explanation: True. Compute Savings Plans are not locked to one instance family the way an EC2 Instance Savings Plan is.

lightning.prompt: On-Demand has no term commitment and is not interrupted when AWS reclaims spare capacity.
lightning.explanation: True. On-Demand is the no-commitment price. Spot is the capacity that can be reclaimed.

lightning.prompt: An S3 gateway endpoint is a target in the route table, and it has no hourly fee.
lightning.explanation: True. You add a route to the gateway endpoint. The endpoint type does not add an hourly charge.

lightning.prompt: The EC2 On-Demand pricing page lists data transfer between instances in the same Availability Zone as free.
lightning.explanation: True. The page says that same-AZ transfer between EC2 instances and elastic network interfaces is free.

lightning.prompt: A CloudFront cache hit is served from the edge location instead of transferring the object from the origin again.
lightning.explanation: True. That is the cache hit. A miss is what still goes to the origin.
